rows.name: API_KEY
rows.values: Any text. The script does not check it.
rows.default: Unset: the script sends the text `YOUR_API_KEY`.
rows.effect: `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server) puts the value in the header `Authorization: Bearer <value>` of every request.
rows.notes: The option `-k` or `--key` overrides the variable.

rows.name: API_URL
rows.values: Full URL of a chat completions endpoint, including the path. `curl` receives the text unchanged.
rows.effect: `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server) posts every request to this URL with `curl`.
rows.notes: The option `-u` or `--url` overrides the variable.

evidence.quote: # POST JSON body $1 to API_URL, passing any extra curl options in $2...

rows.name: CABAL_FLAGS
rows.values: Extra options for `cabal run`, separated by white space. The script splits the text with `str.split()`. Quote characters do not group words.
rows.effect: `build-model.py` (the script that runs ingest for one model) puts the words between `cabal run` and `ingest` in the command that starts the ingest program (the Haskell executable `ingest`). `cabal` is the Haskell build tool.
rows.notes: `build-model.py` reads it only without `--ingest-bin` and `--export-only`. `make build-all-coverage` in `ingest/` sets it to the coverage build options. `ingest/Makefile` assigns its own make variable `CABAL_FLAGS` empty. `make test` ignores a value from the environment.

rows.name: COVERAGE
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns coverage mode on. The script does not parse the text. The value `0` also turns it on.
rows.default: Unset: coverage mode is off. `RUN_COVERAGE` and `COVERAGE_TIX_DIR` are not used.
rows.effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for the models listed in `config/models.yaml`) runs only the models that `RUN_COVERAGE` lists. It sets `HPCTIXFILE` to `<COVERAGE_TIX_DIR>/<model>.tix` for each model. At the end it combines the `.tix` files (Haskell coverage counts) of that directory into `build-all-combined.tix`.
rows.notes: `COVERAGE` adds no coverage option to the `cabal` command. `make build-all-coverage` in `ingest/` sets `COVERAGE=1` and passes those options in `CABAL_FLAGS`. When no `.tix` file exists, the script prints a warning. The CMake option `COVERAGE` is a different setting.

rows.name: COVERAGE_BASELINE
rows.who_sets: CI workflow `ingest-coverage.yml` sets `35`. Developers set it locally.
rows.values: Whole number of percent, for example `35`. The recipe does not check the text. Text that is not an integer makes the recipe print `PASS`.
rows.default: Unset: the recipe stops with a shell error that contains `COVERAGE_BASELINE not set`.
rows.effect: It is the lowest accepted expression coverage of the ingest Haskell code, in percent. The recipe rounds the measured coverage to the nearest 5 percent. The target fails when the rounded value is below the baseline.
rows.notes: Both targets are in `ingest/Makefile`. `coverage-check` reads `coverage-summary.txt` (tests only). `coverage-check-combined` reads `coverage-summary-combined.txt` (tests and `build-all.sh` runs). CI sets `35` and runs `coverage-check-combined`. CI also reports the rounded coverage minus the baseline.

rows.name: COVERAGE_TIX_DIR
rows.values: Path of a directory. A relative path starts at the working directory of the script.
rows.effect: In coverage mode `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for the models listed in `config/models.yaml`) creates the directory. It sets `HPCTIXFILE` to `<directory>/<model>.tix` for each model. At the end it combines all `.tix` files (Haskell coverage counts) of the directory into `build-all-combined.tix`.
rows.notes: Used only when `COVERAGE` is not empty. `.tix` files of an earlier run are combined too. `make build-all-coverage` sets the default directory itself and deletes the `.tix` files there first. `make coverage-combine` reads only `dist-newstyle/coverage/build-all-tix/build-all-combined.tix`. The working directory of the script must be `ingest/`.

rows.name: CPUAFFINITY
rows.who_sets: Nothing in this repository. The unit loads two environment files.
rows.read_by: systemd, when it starts the unit `rinzler@.service` (`packaging/systemd/rinzler@.service`, `packaging/tron-host/90-rinzler-host.conf`)
rows.values: A CPU list in the form that `taskset -c` accepts. `taskset` is the Linux command that starts a program on given CPUs. TRON code does not parse the value.
rows.default: Unset: the unit and the drop-in give no fallback value. No file in this repository sets the variable.
rows.effect: The unit starts rinzler through `/usr/bin/taskset -c <value>`. The rinzler process starts with this CPU list as its affinity. The `tron-host` drop-in starts `rinzler_host` (the rinzler build for CPU inference) the same way.
rows.notes: rinzler binds its application and device threads to its own core sets, for example from `--app-cores` and `--dev-cores`. No TRON code reads the CPU list that `taskset` sets. The unit loads `/etc/rinzler/instance-<id>.env` and the optional `/opt/positron/user/config.env`. A unit comment says platformd writes the first file.

rows.name: DUMP_ALL
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text. The value `0` also turns it on.
rows.default: Unset: off. The script does not add `--dump-all`.
rows.effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for the models listed in `config/models.yaml`) adds `--dump-all` to every `build-model.py` call. The ingest program (the Haskell executable `ingest`) then writes its intermediate representations of each model to files in `ingest/`, for example `<model name>.typedfx`.

evidence.quote: let fname = dumpBaseName options <.> dumpTypeString name

rows.name: EXPORT_ARGS
rows.values: Extra command-line arguments for `build-model.py`. The shell splits the text at white space and expands wildcard characters. Quote characters do not group words.
rows.effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for the models listed in `config/models.yaml`) adds the words to the arguments of every `build-model.py` call.
rows.notes: The words follow `-m`, `--trace-dir` and `--plugin-dir`. The script puts its own options after the words, for example `--meta-device`, `--target-executor` and `--moe-router`. `build-model.py` keeps the last value of a repeated option such as `--target-executor`.

rows.name: EXPORT_DIR
rows.values: Path of a directory. A relative path starts at the working directory of the script.
rows.effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for the models listed in `config/models.yaml`) creates the directory. For each model it passes `<EXPORT_DIR>/<model>` as `--trace-dir` to `build-model.py`. It writes the log of that call to `<EXPORT_DIR>/<model>.log`.

rows.name: EXPORT_ONLY
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text. The value `0` also turns it on.
rows.default: Unset: off. The script does not add `--export-only`.

It does not start the ingest program and does not update the model config file.

rows.name: GHC
rows.who_sets: The Nix dev shell sets `ghc`. CMake sets it for child commands.
rows.values: Name or full path of the GHC program (the Haskell compiler). CMake does not accept a directory.
rows.default: Unset: CMake searches only for `ghc-9.12` and `ghc`, plus `ghc-9.12.2` when `IN_NIX_SHELL` is not defined. `build-model.py` uses `ghc`. Empty: `build-model.py` passes an empty `-w` value.
rows.effect: The two readers differ. CMake configure tries the value as the last candidate name in its search for the compiler, after its fixed names. `build-model.py` passes the value to `cabal run` as the compiler option `-w`.
rows.notes: CMake reads it only with `BUILD_INGEST_MODELS` on and `TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE` empty. A fixed name that CMake finds wins over the value. CMake caches the found path as `GHC_EXECUTABLE`. Without `IN_NIX_SHELL` the compiler must report version 9.12.2. `build-model.py` reads `GHC` only without `--ingest-bin` and `--export-only`.

rows.name: HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN
rows.who_sets: A developer who runs the tree-vis scripts.
rows.values: A Hugging Face access token. Any non-empty text is used unchanged.
rows.default: Unset: the scripts pass no token, unless an earlier source gives one.
rows.effect: The tree-vis scripts (they draw token trees for the KV cache documentation) pass the token to `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` when they load a tokenizer.
rows.notes: It is the last source. `gen.py` first uses `tokenizer.hf_token` of its YAML input, then `HF_TOKEN`. `tokenizer.py` first uses `--hf-token`, then `HF_TOKEN`. No other file in TRON reads this name.

evidence.quote: hf_token = args.hf_token or os.getenv("HF_TOKEN") or os.getenv("HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN")

rows.name: MAX_TOKENS_BASE
rows.values: Whole number of tokens from `1` to `999999999`, without a leading zero. It must be larger than `MAX_TOKENS_JITTER`. Any other value stops the script with exit status 1.
rows.effect: It is the middle of the `max_tokens` range of `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server). Each request gets a random `max_tokens` from base minus jitter to base plus jitter.
rows.notes: The option `-t` or `--max-tokens` overrides the variable. The script header says that long prompt mode needs a server context window of `PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX` plus base plus jitter tokens.

evidence.quote: echo "$var must be a non-negative integer, got '${!var}'" >&2

rows.name: MAX_TOKENS_JITTER
rows.values: Whole number of tokens from `0`, without a leading zero. It must be smaller than `MAX_TOKENS_BASE`. Any other value stops the script with exit status 1.
rows.effect: It is half of the width of the random `max_tokens` range of `burst-test.sh` (the script that sends a burst of chat completion requests to a server). Each request gets a `max_tokens` from base minus jitter to base plus jitter. The value `0` gives every request the base value.
rows.notes: The option `-j` or `--jitter` overrides the variable. Above 16383 tokens the range ends below base plus jitter. The bash variable `RANDOM` gives at most 32767.

evidence.quote: echo "$var must be a non-negative integer, got '${!var}'" >&2

rows.name: NO_META
rows.values: Any non-empty text turns it on. The script does not parse the text. The value `0` also turns it on.
rows.effect: `build-all.sh` (the script that runs ingest for the models listed in `config/models.yaml`) leaves out `--meta-device`. The export step then builds each model with zero-filled weights in CPU memory. With `--meta-device` the parameters stay on the PyTorch meta device (tensors with a shape and no data).

notes: All 17 rows are kept and none is dropped. Every evidence quote is a whole source line without its leading and trailing white space. Rows changed in meaning: CPUAFFINITY, COVERAGE, COVERAGE_TIX_DIR, DUMP_ALL, EXPORT_ARGS, EXPORT_DIR, GHC, MAX_TOKENS_JITTER, NO_META, API_URL, COVERAGE_BASELINE, EXPORT_ONLY. The other rows changed in wording only. The sentence about the empty value was removed from 15 default cells. In these rows an empty value behaves like unset, which the format expresses by the absence of an `Empty:` part. CPUAFFINITY is not a developer tool variable. systemd expands it in the packaged unit `rinzler@.service`. A deployment section fits it better than tools. CPUAFFINITY: the checkout does not show who sets the value, and it does not show what systemd and `taskset` do with an unset value. Five facts rest on tool behaviour and not on checkout text. Each was measured with scratch files outside the checkout. (1) CMake 3.22.1 treats `ENV GHC` inside NAMES as one more candidate name after the listed names. A fixed name on PATH wins over a full path in GHC. A directory, an empty value and an unset variable add nothing. (2) GNU Make 4.3: the assignment `CABAL_FLAGS :=` hides a value from the caller's environment, and the recipe sees an empty value. `make -e` and a command-line assignment are the exceptions. (3) dash and bash: `[ 40 -lt abc ]` prints an error and the else branch runs, so a COVERAGE_BASELINE that is not an integer prints PASS. (4) Python `argparse` keeps the last value of a repeated option, which the EXPORT_ARGS notes use. (5) bash `RANDOM` is at most 32767, which the MAX_TOKENS_JITTER notes use. The term model registry was removed from the cells and from new_terms. The cells name `config/models.yaml`. Source lines with a vertical bar are not quoted: perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh:290 (the curl call, line 284 is quoted), perfetto/tools/burst-test.sh:234 (the value check, line 235 is quoted) and ingest/build-all.sh:132 (the log file).
